why: The inserted fallback made the model prefer later intra-clause cuts that ‘complete the predicate’ (avoiding verb–object splits). That moved the rank-2 position up while slightly lowering rank-1, producing small gains for long-latency bins but removing many early intra-clause cut options that short-latency bins rely on, so harms concentrate in the short bins (notably ≤3/≤7) even though the overall mean is near zero.
lesson: Keep the predicate-completion preference narrowly scoped so it does not eliminate early intra-clause cut options that short-latency budgets need (i.e., avoid suppressing top-1 early cuts while promoting later predicate-completing cuts).
